title: Playing parades: heat, rough streets and reading music
summary: He talks about parades with John Casimir, the heat, stone streets, and playing hymns without reading the music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: What about parades? You've played plenty of parades.
Oh, yeah. I had a couple of pictures of them. Some of them, I didn't know what come of them.
You still play them? Yeah, I still play them.

Play with John. I play with, what you call, this boy, George Williams. You know. Well, I tell you the truth, I'm going to be straight and tell you about them parades. That sun's been a little too hot, man. That didn't use me walking all that hot sun like that. It's hot in that sun, man.

Yeah, it's hot in the summertime. It's hot. In the wintertime, it was cool. I don't mind making it. Man, you know, do you know sometimes you be playing a parade, you know, you can feel that heat come through the caps, to the white caps. You can feel that heat come through that. And it, not, I didn't know you used to be killing myself when I ain't got that to do.
You were talking about this street here used to be rocking.
this would be rocking. Did you ever take parades on the streets like that? Sure, they come through here. Sure, they come through that. How did that affect you when you were marching players?
